desc:
Given a grid matrix and a radius k, build a grid answer of the same shape where answer[i][j] is the sum of all cells matrix[r][c] with |r - i| ≤ k and |c - j| ≤ k. Cells that fall outside the grid are simply ignored, so near the border the neighbourhood is smaller.

matrix = [[1, 2, 3],
          [4, 5, 6],
          [7, 8, 9]], k = 1
answer = [[12, 21, 16],
          [27, 45, 33],
          [24, 39, 28]]
hints: Summing the (2k + 1) x (2k + 1) square around every cell costs up to R * C * k<sup>2</sup>, which is too slow for large k.
Each answer cell is the sum of a rectangle. A 2-D prefix table gives any rectangle sum in O(1).
Clamp the rectangle to the grid: rows max(0, i-k)..min(R-1, i+k) and columns max(0, j-k)..min(C-1, j+k), then evaluate it with the four-term prefix formula.
editorial: Build the prefix table P of size (R + 1) x (C + 1) where P[i][j] is the sum of the top-left i x j block. For each cell (i, j) the neighbourhood is the rectangle with corners (r1, c1) = (max(0, i-k), max(0, j-k)) and (r2, c2) = (min(R-1, i+k), min(C-1, j+k)).
Its sum is P[r2+1][c2+1] - P[r1][c2+1] - P[r2+1][c1] + P[r1][c1]. The clamping handles the border automatically and k larger than the grid just means the whole grid.
Time O(R * C), independent of k, and O(R * C) space for the table and the output.
